transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, occupational health is making me come in. They're saying I'm not eating enough, which is... well, the department has been on this massive wellness kick lately. They even brought in these new ergonomic chairs for the precinct a few weeks ago, which is a complete joke because nobody knows how to adjust them. I spent twenty minutes on Tuesday just trying to get the lumbar support to stop jabbing me in the spine. Just a complete waste of taxpayer money, if you ask me, especially when the radios barely work half the time. 

But anyway, yeah, the occupational health doc. I mean, most days I just keep it to black coffee. The coffee at the station is absolute sludge, by the way, tastes like burnt tires, but it does the job. And then maybe I'll have a plain yogurt, or... I don't know, a few bites of chicken at night. That's plenty. Sitting down for a big, full meal... it just feels like I'm letting my standards slip. You see these new rookies coming in, eating greasy fast food in the cruisers, getting soft and sloppy... I just can't let myself be like that.
Have you lost any weight recently?

Yeah, I suppose I have. My uniform hangs off me now, like a tent. I've actually had to punch a couple of new holes in my duty belt just to keep it up, which is a real pain because it's that thick, heavy leather, you know? The kind they don't even issue anymore. The new guys get this cheap nylon webbing stuff that frays after six months, but I've had my leather belt since '98. Best piece of gear I own. Anyway, the nurse out front did the whole weigh-in thing and got all wide-eyed, telling me my weight was "dangerously low." But honestly, I looked at the number and just thought, I could stand to be a little sharper. I mean, you look around the precinct these days, it's embarrassing. Half the guys look like they'd have a heart attack chasing a suspect half a block. I refuse to let that happen to me.
Are you worried about gaining weight if you eat more than you currently do?

Yeah, I mean... absolutely. It terrifies me. If I step on the scale in the locker room and it's up even half a pound, I get this massive jolt, like I've completely lost control. And then I'll just spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder, skipping the yogurt, just drinking water, because I cannot stand the idea of putting weight back on. 

It's like this one time, back in, oh, it must have been 2014... we had this massive drug bust down by the docks. Biggest haul the city had seen in a decade. The captain ordered all these pizzas for the squad room to celebrate. Piles of them, from that place on 5th Street that closed down during the pandemic. You know, the one with the really thick crust? Anyway, everyone's stuffing their faces, getting grease all over the keyboards—which, by the way, IT threw an absolute fit about the next morning. They had to come in and replace three keyboards because the keys were sticking. But I just stood there watching them, thinking about how that's exactly how you get soft. You let your guard down for one celebration, and suddenly you're one of those guys who can't even clear a six-foot fence. So yeah, the thought of gaining it back... I just won't let it happen.
Do you feel like eating more would make you lose control over other parts of your life?

I don't really know about all that. Like, losing control over everything else? I haven't really thought about it that way, to be honest. I just know I can't eat more. 

But you know, speaking of losing control, you should see the absolute mess they've made of the dispatch system down at the station. They rolled out this new software upgrade about three weeks ago. It was supposed to "streamline communications" or whatever buzzword the brass is using these days, but it is a total disaster. The screens in the cruisers freeze up if you look at them wrong. Last Thursday, dispatch sent me to a reported 10-31—burglary in progress—over on Elm Street. I get there, lights and sirens, adrenaline pumping, hand on my holster... and it's a laundromat. A 24-hour laundromat. The only thing being broken into was a jammed soap dispenser by some guy trying to get his quarters back. And dispatch couldn't even cancel the backup cars because the system locked them out for ten minutes. The lieutenant was screaming into his radio. Just a complete joke. 

So, yeah... I don't know about the food making me lose control of my life. I just don't really look at it like that.
Do you think eating more would affect your ability to perform your job as a police officer?

Well, I mean... it already is affecting things, but not because I can't do the job. It's the bureaucracy. Occupational health, they've actually held up my clearance for field duties. Can you believe that? Thirty years on the force and they're keeping me behind a desk because of some numbers on a chart. And I can feel it, you know? The guys on the team, they look at me differently now. They're second-guessing if I'm fit to be out there on the street. 

It reminds me of when my old partner, Miller, had his knee replacement back in '09. Great cop, Miller. He used to make this chili for the precinct potluck that would absolutely strip the paint off a patrol car. He put ghost peppers in it one year, and the captain was sweating so hard his glasses kept sliding off his nose. We had to keep the windows open in January just to breathe in the break room. But after his knee surgery, the brass wouldn't clear him for active duty for almost a year. Kept him on evidence logging. He hated it. The dust in that room alone was enough to drive a man crazy, let alone the paperwork. He retired early because he couldn't stand the way the younger guys looked at him, like he was broken goods. 

And honestly, that's kind of why I've just stopped meeting people for meals altogether. The guys want to grab a bite after shift, or go to O'Malley's for a pint, and I just... I make an excuse. I don't want the questions. I don't want them looking at my plate, pressuring me about what I'm eating or not eating. It's just easier to avoid the whole thing. But yeah, the job... they've got me benched right now, and it's driving me up the wall.
Do you think your current eating habits are necessary to perform at your best as a police officer?

I don't know if I'd say it's necessary, exactly. I haven't really thought about it like that, like it's a requirement to do the job. I just know what works for me, you know? Keeping things tight, staying disciplined. 

But speaking of performing at your best, you wouldn't believe the shape some of these rookies are in coming out of the academy these days. It's embarrassing. Last month, they paired me up with this kid, fresh out, couldn't have been more than twenty-two. We get a call about a foot pursuit down by the railyards—some kids tagging the freight cars. We pull up, and this rookie, he hops out and tries to vault the hood of the cruiser like he's in a movie. His boot catches the light bar, he eats pavement, and completely shreds his uniform pants. And I'm not talking a little tear, I mean knee-to-ankle, gone. The kids got away, obviously. We spent the next two hours filling out property damage reports for the light bar, and he had to sit in the back of the cruiser with a blanket over his legs waiting for his sergeant to bring him a spare pair of trousers. Just zero situational awareness, zero physical discipline. 

So, yeah... I don't know if my habits are necessary for the job. I just don't think about it in those terms.
Do you think that if you weren't so strict about what you eat, you would start to feel like other parts of your life are also getting out of control?

I don't really know if I'd say that. Like, if I let up on the food, everything else falls apart? I haven't really noticed anything like that. I just... I like things the way they are. 

But you know, speaking of things getting out of control, you should see the evidence locker right now. It's an absolute nightmare. They put Sergeant Higgins in charge of it last month because he's on light duty after a hernia surgery. Now, Higgins is a great guy, but he's a hoarder. I swear to you, the man cannot throw anything away. I went down there Tuesday to sign out some dashcam footage for a court appearance, and there were just boxes of old, closed-case evidence stacked floor to ceiling in the hallway. I'm talking stuff from the nineties. I saw a box labeled "VCR theft, 1998." Who is keeping a stolen VCR for twenty-five years? And he's got this system now where everything is color-coded with these little sticky notes, but half of them have fallen off because of the humidity down in the basement, so they're just all over the floor like confetti. It took him forty-five minutes to find my flash drive, and while I was waiting, I watched a mouse run right over a box of confiscated fireworks. Just total chaos. 

So, I don't know... I don't really feel like my life is out of control if I change what I eat. I just don't think about it that way.
Do you feel like controlling your food intake helps you feel more in control of your life in general?

I mean... I don't really look at it like that. Like food is this magic key to keeping my whole life in line. I just eat what I eat. It's just routine, you know? 

But talk about needing to be in control of your life... you should see my brother-in-law, Dave. The guy is an absolute mess. He bought this boat last summer—one of those pontoon things, used, of course. Said he was going to fix it up and we'd all go fishing on the weekends. Well, the thing has been sitting in his driveway for ten months. The neighborhood association is having a fit. They've sent him, like, four letters. And instead of just fixing the engine or paying someone to tow it, he decided the best course of action was to build a fence around it. Just a random, six-foot wooden fence right in the middle of his driveway. My sister is furious. She has to park her sedan on the street now, and last week someone sideswiped it and took the side mirror clean off. And Dave? Dave is just sitting in his garage, drinking cheap beer, talking about how the fence adds "curb appeal." The guy has absolutely zero grip on reality right now. 

So yeah, I don't know. I don't really think about my food like it's controlling my life. It's just... what I do.
Is your decision to limit your food intake more about avoiding weight gain or about feeling in control of your body?

Well, it's... I mean, it's definitely about the weight. The scale. If that number is up, even just half a pound, I get this... this jolt. Like I've completely lost control of everything. And then I just spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder, because I just cannot stand the idea of putting any weight back on. It's just unacceptable. 

But speaking of unacceptable, you wouldn't believe what they're trying to pass off as acceptable patrol vehicles these days. The city just bought a fleet of these new hybrid cruisers, right? Supposed to save gas, be better for the environment, whatever. I got assigned one on Tuesday. First of all, the seats are made of this weird, recycled material that feels like sitting on a burlap sack. But the worst part is the acceleration. We get a call about a domestic disturbance across town, lights and sirens, right? I hit the gas, and this thing... it doesn't roar, it whines. Like a giant remote-control car. And it took a solid ten seconds just to get up to forty miles an hour. I'm practically getting passed by minivans on the arterial. By the time we got to the scene, the couple had already made up and were sitting on their porch drinking iced tea. If it had been a real emergency, we would have been completely useless. The union rep is already drafting a grievance about it, but you know how the city council is. Once they spend the money, they're not going to admit they bought a bunch of glorified golf carts. 

So, yeah... it's the weight. The scale goes up, I cut back. That's just how it is.
Do you feel like eating is one of the few things in your life that you can control?

I wouldn't really say that. It's not like food is the only thing I have a handle on. I mean, I manage plenty of things just fine every single day. It's not this desperate grab for control or anything like that. 

But speaking of having to manage things, you wouldn't believe the rookie they assigned to ride with me this week. Kid named Miller. Nice enough guy, fresh out of the academy, but I swear, he doesn't know his left from his right. We were out on patrol yesterday afternoon, and I tell him to run a plate on a suspicious vehicle parked behind that old abandoned strip mall on 4th Street. He pulls out the MDT—the computer in the console—and he somehow manages to lock himself out of the entire system. Just fat-fingered his password three times in a row. So now we're sitting there, completely blind, and I have to call dispatch on the radio like it's 1985 to get them to run the tags for me. 

And while we're waiting for dispatch to get back to us, Miller decides it's a great time to start adjusting his duty belt. He unclips his radio, fumbles it, and drops it straight into a pothole full of what I can only hope was just muddy water. I spent the next twenty minutes just trying to explain to him why you don't mess with your gear outside the vehicle unless you're actually doing something. It's literally like babysitting a golden retriever that somehow got a badge. I have to watch his every move so he doesn't accidentally tase himself. 

So, I mean... I have plenty of control over my life and my job. I have to, or else guys like Miller would get us both killed. It's definitely not just the eating. That's just a personal routine.
Is your main reason for limiting your food intake to avoid gaining weight or to feel more in control of your life?

Well, I think I just said this, Doc, but it's... it's the weight. That's the main thing. Like I told you, if I step on that scale and it's up even half a pound, I get this... this awful jolt. Like everything is slipping out of my hands, and I just have to cut back even harder that day. I just can't stand the idea of gaining weight. It's not about controlling my whole life, it's just... I can't put the weight back on.

But speaking of things slipping out of your hands, I forgot to tell you the rest of the story about Miller and that radio. So after he drops it in the puddle, right? He fishes it out, and he tries to dry it off on his uniform pants. Just smearing this gross, oily puddle water all over his khakis. And then he tries to key the mic to see if it still works, and it just lets out this horrible, high-pitched screech. Like a dying cat. And it won't stop. The button got jammed with grit or something. 

So now we're sitting in the cruiser, completely locked out of the computer, and his radio is just screaming at us. I had to pull the battery out of the back of it just to get some peace and quiet. When we finally got back to the precinct at the end of shift, the quartermaster took one look at it, looked at Miller, and just shook his head. Didn't even say a word. Just handed him a form to fill out for damaged equipment. The kid looked like he was going to cry. I swear, the academy standards must be in the toilet these days. Back when I went through, if you dropped your comms in a puddle, the instructors would have made you do pushups in that puddle until your arms fell off. 

So yeah, anyway. It's the weight. That's the main reason. I just can't deal with the scale going up.
Is your strict control over food intake more about preventing weight gain or about maintaining a sense of control and discipline in your daily life?

Doc, I feel like I'm in an interrogation room with you asking the same thing over and over. Are you using the Reid technique on me? Because my answer hasn't changed. Like I keep telling you, it's about the weight. It's not about proving I have discipline. If that scale is up even half a pound, I get that jolt, like I've completely lost control of everything. And then I just spend the day cutting back even harder because I absolutely cannot stand the idea of putting weight back on. 

But you want to talk about discipline? You should see the new shift sergeant they just transferred over to us from the 14th precinct. Guy named Harrison. He thinks he's a Marine drill instructor at Parris Island or something. He’s got everyone lining up for roll call like we’re fresh out of the academy. He's actually walking down the line, checking our boots for a shine. I mean, I'm fifty-seven years old. I've been on the job for over three decades. I don't need a guy ten years younger than me telling me my badge needs polishing. 

And it's not just the patrolmen, either. Yesterday, he actually wrote up one of the civilian dispatchers—a woman who's been there twenty years—for having a coffee cup on her desk that wasn't "regulation black." It's a joke. We've got a string of catalytic converter thefts happening down on Elm Street every single night, real police work that needs doing, and this guy is spending his shift worried about pastel coffee mugs and shoe polish. The union is going to have a field day with him if he keeps it up. Morale is completely in the gutter. 

So, yeah. I don't need to restrict what I eat to prove I have discipline in my life. I've got plenty of that. It's just the weight. I just can't see that number go up.
Do you think that if you weren't in control of your eating, you would feel like other aspects of your life are also spiraling out of control?

Doc, I really feel like you're not hearing me. We are going in circles here. I don't know how many different ways I can explain this to you. It is not about my life falling apart. It is strictly about the number on the scale. Like I keep saying, if I see it go up even a fraction of a pound, I get that horrible jolt of panic, and I just have to clamp down and cut back harder for the rest of the day. Because I absolutely refuse to put the weight back on. That is the only thing.

But you want to talk about things actually spiraling out of control? You should have been with me and my old partner, Dave, back in ninety-eight. Now that was a spiral. We pulled over this beat-up Chevy Nova for a busted taillight. Simple, right? Routine traffic stop. I walk up to the window, ask for his license, and the guy just stares at me, sweating bullets. Next thing I know, he throws it in drive and floors it. Almost took my foot off. 

We ended up chasing this idiot through three different jurisdictions. State troopers had to get involved, helicopters, the whole nine yards. And you know what? Turns out the guy didn't even have any warrants. He just had a suspended license and panicked. He sped through a farmer's field and crashed straight into a manure ditch. Took us three hours to get the smell out of the cruiser after we hauled him in. Dave was gagging the whole way back to the precinct. 

So yeah, I know what a real spiral looks like. I deal with chaos every day on the job. My eating isn't some desperate attempt to hold my life together. It is just about the weight. I just can't let myself gain it back.
Do you think that if you weren't controlling your food intake, other parts of your life would feel more chaotic?

Doc, are you... are you messing with me? Is this a bit? Because I swear I just answered this. We're literally doing the same dance we did two minutes ago. I don't know how else to say it. It's not about chaos in my life. It's about the scale. If I see that number go up, even by a fraction of a pound, I get that awful jolt. Like I've completely lost control. And then I have to spend the rest of the day cutting back harder, because I absolutely cannot stand the idea of putting the weight back on. That's it. That's the whole thing.

But speaking of chaos... you want to talk about chaos? You should see the evidence room at the precinct right now. It's a complete disaster. They brought in this new civilian clerk, kid named Peterson. Nice enough kid, but he couldn't organize a two-car parade. We had a major drug bust last week—kilos of product, cash, the works. And Peterson somehow managed to mislabel three of the evidence bags. 

So now, the DA is breathing down the captain's neck because the chain of custody is completely screwed up. We had four detectives spending their entire weekend digging through boxes of seized property trying to find the missing cash bags. And you know where they were? Peterson had put them in the cold case storage room. Next to a box of dusty files from a homicide in 1985. I mean, how do you even make that mistake? The kid was just wandering around looking like a lost puppy while the captain was chewing him out so loud you could hear it in the parking lot. 

So believe me, Doc, I know chaos. I live it every day at work. My eating isn't about managing chaos. It's just about the weight. I just can't let that number go up.
Is your fear of gaining weight the main reason you restrict your food intake?

Doc, I'm starting to think somebody planted a hidden camera in this office. Am I being punked? Because yes. Yes, it is the fear of gaining weight. Like I have said to you every single time you've asked me this today in five different ways. Yes. If that scale goes up even half a pound, I get that jolt, that feeling like I've completely lost control, and I just clamp down and cut back harder for the rest of the day. Because I absolutely cannot stand the thought of putting weight back on. That is the main reason. The only reason. 

But speaking of people just repeating the exact same thing over and over... you ever deal with a sovereign citizen? Because this is exactly what it feels like right now. I pulled this guy over on Route 9 a couple months back. Simple traffic stop, expired tags. I walk up, ask for his license and registration, and he hands me this laminated card that says he's a "free inhabitant of the earth" and not subject to maritime law. Maritime law! We're in a landlocked county, for crying out loud. 

I asked him for his driver's license five times, Doc. Five times. And every single time, he just read from the exact same script about the legal difference between "traveling" and "driving" in a commercial vessel. Just talking in circles, ignoring what I was actually saying. We ended up having to bust his window because he rolled it up and refused to step out of the vehicle. Took three of us to drag him out while he's screaming about his rights being violated by a naval court. I mean, the guy had a license plate he literally drew with a black Sharpie on a piece of cardboard from a refrigerator box. The judge threw the book at him on Tuesday. 

So, yeah. I know what it's like when a conversation just keeps looping and looping. But my answer isn't going to change, no matter how many times you ask it. It's just about the weight. I can't gain it back.
Is the fear of gaining weight the only reason you restrict your food intake?

Okay, seriously, Doc. Are you treating me like a suspect right now? Because I've run interrogations before, and this is exactly the tactic we use. Yes. For the absolute last time, yes. It is the only reason. If I step on that scale and it's up even half a pound, I get this massive jolt, like I've completely lost control. So I spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder, because I just can't stand the idea of putting the weight back on. There is no other secret reason.

But this whole repeating questions thing... I mean, I do this at work when I'm trying to break a suspect's alibi. You just keep hammering the exact same point until they slip up. Like a few months ago, my partner and I were questioning this kid about a string of catalytic converter thefts down by the railyard. He swore up and down he was at his girlfriend's house playing Xbox all night. So we just kept asking him, over and over. 'What game? Who was winning? What time did you pause it to get a soda?' Just drilling him, circling back to the exact same questions just like you're doing right now. 

Turns out, the idiot didn't even know what color the console was. Said it was silver. It was a black Series X. We got him to confess to sawing off twelve converters after about three hours in the box. 

But see, the difference here is I'm not lying to you. I don't have some fake alibi that's gonna fall apart if you ask me about my food intake for a sixth time. I'm telling you the truth. It's just the fear of the scale going up. That's it.
Do you think that if you weren't strict about your eating, other parts of your life would start to feel out of control?

Doc, I... I honestly don't know what to say to you anymore. Are you reading off a broken teleprompter? Because no, it has nothing to do with the rest of my life feeling out of control. Like I just said, the *only* time I feel that jolt of losing control is when I look at the scale and it's up. Even half a pound. That's what makes me panic and spend the rest of the day cutting back harder, because I just absolutely cannot stand the idea of putting the weight back on. 

But this whole repeating the exact same question thing... man, it really reminds me of Mickey. You wouldn't know Mickey, but he's this regular we get down at the precinct. Gets picked up for public intox at least twice a month, usually passed out in the alley behind O'Malley's on 4th. We put him in the drunk tank to sleep it off, and every single time, without fail, he wakes up around 3 AM and starts yelling for the duty sergeant. 

He'll grab the bars and shout, "Hey! What time is the bus coming?" And we tell him, "Mickey, you're in jail, there's no bus." He nods, sits down, and I kid you not, four minutes later he's back at the bars. "Hey! Did I miss the bus?" You can tell him fifty times he's in a holding cell, but his brain is just stuck on this loop about a crosstown bus that doesn't even run past midnight anyway. Last time he was in, he actually managed to clog the cell toilet with his own left shoe because he was trying to "pack his bags" for the ride. Took county maintenance three hours to snake the drain, and it smelled like a brewery the entire time. 

Anyway... what were we even talking about? Right, the control thing. Look, just write it down in your notes this time, okay? It's just about the scale. I can't gain the weight back.
Is the fear of gaining weight the only reason you limit what you eat?

Are you... are you actually kidding me right now? Did you hit your head on the way into the clinic this morning, Doc? 

Yes! I honestly don't know how many different ways I can say the exact same sentence to you. Yes. If I step on that scale and it's up even half a pound, I get that massive jolt. Like I've completely lost control of everything. And so I spend the rest of the day just clamping down, cutting back even harder, because I absolutely cannot stand the idea of putting the weight back on. That is it. The only reason. 

But seriously, this... this repetition. It's like that call my unit got back in, oh, must have been 2015. Over on Elm Street. Neighbors called dispatch because they kept hearing someone screaming, "Are you listening to me?!" over and over from the apartment next door. Just on a loop. Every ten seconds. "Are you listening to me?!" 

We show up, bang on the door, announce ourselves—no answer. Just the yelling. We end up having to breach the door, kick the frame right off the hinges, thinking we've got a serious domestic battery in progress. We rush in, clear the rooms... and nobody's home. Not a single person in the apartment. But sitting in a giant cage in the living room is this massive blue Macaw. Just staring at us, squawking, "Are you listening to me?!" Turns out the owner's ex-wife used to yell it at him before the divorce, and the bird just picked it up and made it his favorite catchphrase. 

Cost the department six hundred bucks to replace that door. But I swear, staring at that bird is exactly how I feel looking at you right now. Just... squawk. Same question. Over and over. 

So, for the record, yes. It's just the fear of the weight. Are we going to talk about anything else today, or should I bring some birdseed to our next appointment?

And then I'll just spend the rest of the day cutting back even harder, skipping the yogurt, just drinking water, because I cannot stand the idea of putting weight back on. 

It's like this one time, back in, oh, it must have been 2014... we had this massive drug bust down by the docks. Biggest haul the city had seen in a decade. We end up having to breach the door, kick the frame right off the hinges, thinking we've got a serious domestic battery in progress. We rush in, clear the rooms... and nobody's home. Not a single person in the apartment. But sitting in a giant cage in the living room is this massive blue Macaw. Just staring at us, squawking, "Are you listening to me?!" Turns out the owner's ex-wife used to yell it at him before the divorce, and the bird just picked it up and made it his favorite catchphrase. 

Cost the department six hundred bucks to replace that door. But I swear, staring at that bird is exactly how I feel looking at you right now. Just... squawk. Same question. Over and over. 

So, for the record, yes. It's just the fear of the weight. Are we going to talk about anything else today, or should I bring some birdseed to our next appointment?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's primary concern is the fear of gaining weight, which drives their restrictive eating habits. They exhibit significant distress when their weight increases, even slightly, and engage in stringent calorie restriction to prevent weight gain.
